subtitle: A 250-metre surf beach in Sydney's east whose lifesaving club calls itself the oldest in the world, a 1903 claim the sport's own historians have never been able to verify.
spike_statement: Bronte's surf club calls itself the world's oldest, founded 1903, but no primary record proves it; Bondi's 1907 founding is the earliest documented.

levers.photo_tone: Warm sandstone headlands framing a short surf beach, the 30-metre Bronte Baths cut into the rock at the south end, the green bowl of Bronte Park and its Norfolk pines behind the sand, morning light off an exposed swell
